newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slides with NY, May premium sold.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slides with NY, May premium sold.

text.p: White sugar futures headed lower in tandem with the weakness in New York but sellers were lurking in the wings to prevent the May arbitrage from widening too far, traders said on Wednesday.
The London market showed a marked reluctance to trade earlier in the day and although some trade selling was noted the nearby values remained in a narrow range.
"There was a bit of selling against the EU (tender) but there was good buying in the whites just before New opened," said one trader.
"But since then there's been some pressure even though the premium has widened -- really we haven't moved that much," he said, noting premium selling at $69.
At 1635 GMT May was down $1.10 at $307.00 and August down $1.60 at $305.50, with May/August also widening from Tuesday's close of $1.00. Sellers were mixed.
Overall turnover amounted to a thin 948 lots.
"London volume is very light, there's not much around," the trader said.
In physical news, Iran bought another cargo of white sugar at around $314.00, the same price as the cargo bought last week and from the same supplier.
The Paris market was more active than usual and Matif volume reached 735 lots. May was down $1.00 at $306.00 and August unchanged at $306.30.
